sites.name: Cod Hole - Ribbon No 10 Reef - GBR

s1.quote: Cod Hole, located on Ribbon Reef Number 10 near the northern end of the chain … The dive site itself is a coral garden at 16 to 18 metres, with sandy channels between the formations

s2.quote: Potato cod at Cod Hole reach 1.5 to 2 metres in length … The Ribbon Reefs are accessible only by liveaboard from Cairns.

s3.quote: Cod Hole, as the name suggests, is a dive site famous for cod; giant Queensland grouper to be exact.

highlights.text: Habituated giant potato cod (up to 2 m)

summary.text: Ribbon Reef 10 coral garden at about 16-18 m, famous for the giant potato cod that approach divers. Reached only by multi-day liveaboard from Cairns.

s1.quote: Steve’s Bommie on Ribbon Reef 3 is a pinnacle rising from 30 metres to within a few metres of the surface, encrusted with soft corals and surrounded by schooling fish

s2.quote: A memorial plaque can be seen at 25m where most scuba divers start on this site … Steve's Bommie features a wealth of schooling action, big fish and macro life. Cruising barracudas, whitetip reef sharks

highlights.text: Schooling fish, barracuda, whitetip reef sharks

summary.text: A pinnacle on Ribbon Reef 3 rising from around 30 m to just below the surface, with divers often starting near 25 m. Known for schooling fish, big predators and macro life.

s1.quote: Depth: Top: 8M Median: 13M Bottom: 18M … It is a crack / arch in the rock in an inverted V shape … swimming through it with grey nurse sharks is one of the best dives in the NSW North patch

s2.quote: The maximum depth in the trench varies from 16 metres on the western side to 21 on the east. Grey nurse sharks often congregate in the Looking Glass

s3.quote: Looking Glass is affected by even moderate seas and can easily become extremely surgey and undiveable.

highlights.text: Swim-through gap with grey nurse sharks

hazards.text: Surge; undiveable in even moderate seas

summary.text: A trench or arch cutting through the rock at Broughton Island, shallowest inside the gap, where grey nurse sharks gather. Dives only when seas are calm as surge builds quickly.

s1.quote: You can snorkel at various locations in the Sanctuary. Most of the area is shallow water of less than five metres, providing an easily accessible recreational area for snorkeling

s2.quote: Fifty-one species of fish have been identified, the most common being rays, southern hulafish, zebra fish, dusky morwongs, moonlighters and Australian sweep.

s3.quote: Ricketts Point is a great location for visitors to snorkel and scuba dive to experience the diverse marine life in Port Phillip Bay.

highlights.text: Rays, southern hulafish, zebra fish, morwongs

summary.text: A shallow marine sanctuary in Port Phillip Bay, mostly under 5 m, suited to snorkelling and scuba with rockpools close to shore and about fifty fish species recorded.

s1.quote: Tinderbox Marine Nature Reserve is the perfect place for adults and children who are learning to snorkel or scuba dive … divers frequently find themselves amongst bigbelly seahorses, rock lobsters and wrasse

s2.quote: Ideal for divers of all levels, the reserve offers clear waters and calm conditions, making it a perfect spot for both exploration and underwater photography.

highlights.text: Bigbelly seahorses, rock lobsters, weedy seadragons

summary.text: South of Hobart marine reserve with rocky reef, kelp and sand, suited to beginners and photographers, with calm clear water and seahorses and seadragons.

s1.quote: the wharf is best saved for the end of a dive. The main feature of this site is a rocky reef that quickly drops to the sand line at 16m.

s2.quote: Merimbula Wharf is a great spot to dive at any time of the year, with the visibility generally 8m to 12m, but over 15m at times. Entry and exits can be a little tricky over the rocks

s3.quote: the main stars are the large blue groper wrasse that follow divers around until they are fed a sea urchin

hazards.text: Tricky rock entry; avoid in southerly swell

s1.quote: Located 22 nautical miles offshore, conditions have to be perfect to visit this rocky reef that rises from 50 metres to 22 metres. A dive for experienced divers only

s2.quote: Schooling pelagic fish gather at Barwon Banks, with masses of barracuda, trevally, rainbow runners and batfish swarming around divers.

s1.quote: Asho’s Gap (12 meters max) where there is a reef shark cleaning station frequented by Grey Reef Sharks that line up to have their teeth cleaned by cleaner wrasse
Cabbage Patch 6-27 m | -12.0946, 96.8422 Enter a world of beautiful green and gold cabbage shaped coral … Look out for curious and shy spotted garden eels here too, and sleeping white tip reef sharks
